messages:
sam: Installer on my WSL2 Ubuntu added lines to both ~/.bashrc and ~/.profile during postinstall. After that, `redwoodctl login` gets stuck in an auth retry loop when I start `redwoodctl localserve` — it keeps printing `auth: retrying` and never finishes. Anyone seen this?

maria: Can you paste the installer output and the exact lines that were added? Sounds like duplicate sourcing.

sam: Sure — installer output looked normal. The problem blocks are identical in both files. From ~/.bashrc:
```
# redwoodctl init
source ~/.redwood/profile
export REDWOOD_PROFILE=default
```
and ~/.profile has the same three lines appended.

jonathan: Double-sourcing could spawn multiple auth agents or re-run init twice. What does `redwoodctl auth status` show?

sam: `redwoodctl auth status` reports `auth: pending`. `ps aux | grep redwood` shows two auth-agent processes. Logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:33Z] auth-agent starting
[2026-03-15T10:12:33Z] opening device for user token
[2026-03-15T10:12:35Z] auth: retrying (err: device busy)
```

ali: I bumped into something similar — on WSL the distro often sources multiple rc files, so postinstall must be idempotent. Workaround: remove one of the blocks (I removed the one from ~/.profile) or guard with an env var: `if [ -z \"$REDWOOD_INIT_DONE\" ]; then export REDWOOD_INIT_DONE=1; source ~/.redwood/profile; fi`.

maria: Another pattern is to create a marker file like `~/.redwood/initialized` after first init and check for it before re-running.

sam: Removing the duplicate from ~/.profile fixed it for me — login completed afterwards. But this will hit new users during onboarding (bad first impression).

devex-bot: @sam thanks for reporting. Filed DX ticket #DX-4897: "installer: avoid duplicate shell-init on WSL / add idempotent guard + marker file". Assigned to @maria and @jonathan.

jonathan: Proposed fix: change postinstall to detect interactive shell and append only to the most appropriate rc (prefer ~/.bashrc for bash, ~/.zshrc for zsh). Also add a guard around the block: `if [ -f ~/.redwood/initialized ]; then return; fi; touch ~/.redwood/initialized`.

maria: Also add a tiny migration utility that runs on startup to dedupe existing rc files if we detect multiple redwood blocks. We should also log a friendly message when duplicates are found: "Detected multiple redwoodctl init blocks — run `redwoodctl diagnose-init` to fix".

ali: For an immediate UX patch we can update the installer notice: if we detect WSL, warn users that their distro may source multiple files and we only add to one; include a link to the diagnosis command in the output.

sam: I'll paste repro steps in the ticket: OS: WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04, shell: bash, installer: homebrew cask, redwoodctl v0.9.3. Also attached both rc files.

maria: Great, thanks — we'll prioritize this for the next patch. @jonathan can you add the dedicate test for WSL in the postinstall integration tests?

jonathan: Yep — adding integration test + unit to ensure idempotency.

sam: Thanks all, saved me an afternoon :relieved:

maria: Can you update the ticket with the exact process you used to remove the duplicate so support can reference it? Short snippet is fine: `grep -n \"redwoodctl init\" ~/.bashrc ~/.profile` then manually remove one block.

sam: Done, added exact commands and logs to DX-4897. Closing the loop once patch is released. :thumbsup:
